On success you get 200 JSON: read count and iterate articles[] (each has title, url, domain, source_country, language, seendate ISO timestamp, socialimage), and use breakdowns for aggregate coverage (top_source_countries, top_domains, languages). The compiled 'query' and 'filters' fields show exactly what GDELT was asked. entries.name: Agentstools News Search

backends.outputSchema: { query (string, echoed), count (integer), results[]: { title (string), url (string), snippet (string), date (ISO 8601 string), source (string — publication name), image (string url, may be empty) } }

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/search/news?query=ethereum%20etf&max_results=5&timelimit=w (query REQUIRED; max_results/timelimit/region/safesearch/backend optional; all query-string params, no request body)

max_results is capped at 20 (enum 1-20).
timelimit is a single-letter freshness enum: d/w/m/y (past day/week/month/year).
An empty or upstream-blocked result is a valid HTTP 200 with count:0 and results:[] — never a 500; treat count:0 as 'no news', not an error.
results[].image can be an empty string when the engine returns no thumbnail.
Covers ANY topic (not only crypto); distinct from the provider's /search (generic web search) and /gdelt/news (GDELT event corpus).
Price $0.003 USDC on Base (eip155:8453); no API key.
usage.guide: Search recent news headlines by keyword across web news engines (Bing, DuckDuckGo, Yahoo via ddgs). entries.name: OpenWebNinja News Search

query.description: Search query for which to get news. REQUIRED.

limit.description: Maximum number of news articles to return.

time_published.description: Find news articles published in a specific time range (e.g. anytime, 1h, 1d, 7d, 1y).

source.description: Domain of the source from which to return news articles (e.g. bbc.com).

language.description: Language of the results (ISO 639-1 alpha-2). Default en.

data.description: News article results matching the query, each { article_id, title, link, snippet, photo_url, thumbnail_url, published_datetime_utc, authors[], source_url, source_name, source_logo_url, source_favicon_url, source_publication_id, related_topics[], sub_articles[], story_id }.

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.openwebninja.com/realtime-news-data/search with REQUIRED query param query (the news search keywords) and optional limit (default 10, 1-500), time_published (default anytime), source (source domain), country (ISO alpha-2, default us), language (ISO 639-1 alpha-2, default en). time_published narrows the recency window (e.g. anytime, 1h, 1d, 7d, 1y); source scopes results to one publisher domain.

entries.name: Agentstools Product Safety Recall
entries.description: Checks a consumer good, food, drug or medical device by brand or product name against US recall registries, fusing CPSC and openFDA recalls into one cited JSON with hazard, FDA class, remedy, status and a deterministic risk score (risk indicators, not advice).

query.description: Brand or product name to search, e.g. 'Fisher-Price stroller' or 'peanut butter'.

domain.description: Which recall registries to search (default all): consumer=CPSC, food/drug/device=openFDA.

partial.description: True if one or more upstream registries failed for this query.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/safety/product?query=<brand or product name>[&domain=<all|consumer|food|drug|device>][&limit=<1-50>] — all inputs are query params, no request body; only query is meaningful (domain defaults to all, limit to 20). Result is inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: query{query,domain} echo, matched_count (int), matched_recalls[] (each: source (cpsc|openfda_food|openfda_drug|openfda_device), classification (FDA class), status, date, hazard, match_score), risk_score{score, band (low|medium|high), flags{has_recall, has_active_recall, max_fda_classification, hazard_mentions_death, hazard_mentions_injury}, reasons[], signals{...}}, sources{providers[], partial (bool), errors{per-provider}}, attribution[] (CPSC + openFDA), disclaimer.
quirks: All params are optional query-string values (no body); pass query=<brand or product name>. domain selects registries (all|consumer=CPSC|food|drug|device=openFDA), defaults to all; limit (1-50) caps matched_recalls, default 20.
Fuses U.S. CPSC (saferproducts.gov) and openFDA (open.fda.gov) recall data into one response with a deterministic risk_score — it returns risk INDICATORS, not safety advice (see disclaimer).

sources.partial=true with per-provider strings in sources.errors when an upstream registry fails; at index time (2026-08-07) the three openFDA registries returned 'upstream api.fda.gov returned HTTP 403' (openFDA rate/anti-bot) while CPSC still ran — the Agentstools endpoint itself still returned its full documented shape (same upstream-FDA-403 behavior as the sibling drug/shortages op).
matched_count can be 0 with an empty matched_recalls[] when no recall matches (risk_score.score 0, band 'low') — verified live: query='Fisher-Price stroller' returned matched_count 0, band low.
Absence of a recall is not proof of safety (per the response disclaimer).
usage.guide: Screen a product, food, drug or medical device for US recalls with a single keyless x402 GET. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/safety/product?query=<brand or product name> with an optional domain (all|consumer|food|drug|device, default all) and limit (1-50, default 20). No request body. Pays $0.02 USDC via x402 on Base. Synchronous — the 200 body carries matched_recalls[] (each with source, FDA classification, status, date, hazard, match_score), a deterministic risk_score{score, band, flags, reasons}, plus sources{providers, partial, errors} and CPSC/openFDA attribution. Fuses CPSC + openFDA recalls into one cited JSON; check sources.partial for degraded upstreams. Use for consumer-product / food / drug / device recall and safety-risk screening by brand or product name.

entries.name: Agentstools Crime Agency
entries.description: Normalized crime profile for one FBI reporting agency by ORI code: give an ORI (and optionally an offense and a window of years) and get the agency's multi-year annualized offense rates per 100,000 people, the latest complete reporting year, the trend and the data as-of date — the raw agency grain behind crime/location, no geocoding.

ori.description: FBI agency ORI code (e.g. DE0010100). Required.

verdict.description: found | unavailable (unavailable when the upstream FBI source is down; result may be partial).

trend_pct.description: Percent change from the earliest to the latest complete year.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/crime/agency with query params: ori (FBI ORI code, REQUIRED, e.g. DE0010100); optional offense (one of violent-crime|homicide|rape|robbery|aggravated-assault|property-crime|burglary|larceny|motor-vehicle-theft|arson, default violent-crime); optional years (trailing reporting years 1-10, default 5). No request body. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result is returned inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).
usage.outputShape: verdict (found|unavailable); ori; offense; offense_label; agency.{ori,agency_name,agency_type,state,state_name,counties[],is_nibrs,matched_address,resolution_mode}; annual_rates[].{year,rate_per_100k_yr,complete}; trend_pct (% change earliest->latest complete year); as_of (MM/YYYY); window.{from,to}; sources.{errors,partial}; attribution[]; ethics; disclaimer; ts.
quirks: All input is query params (no request body). ori is required; agents that already hold an FBI ORI use this raw-agency grain, whereas the sibling crime/location adds a geocode step on top.
Sibling ops on the same host are DISTINCT operations, not aliases: crime/location (geocoded lookup that resolves to agencies) and crime/incidents (incident-level query). Do not collapse.

Partial-success mode: when upstream FBI Crime Data Explorer is briefly down it returns verdict='unavailable' with sources.partial=true and sources.errors populated (e.g. 'upstream FBI returned HTTP 403') and an empty annual_rates[] rather than failing. Observed live at index time: paid HTTP 200 for ori=DE0010100 but FBI CDE returned 403 so annual_rates was empty; the OpenAPI example (verdict='found', Dover Police Department DE, 2023 rate 640.2/100k, trend +4.1%, as_of 06/2026) shows the fully-populated shape.
An agency with no data in the requested window returns an empty annual_rates[] even when the source is up.

United States only. Source is the FBI Crime Data Explorer (UCR/NIBRS summarized data, US DOJ, api.usa.gov/crime/fbi/cde; US-gov public domain). Data lags 1-2 years and reporting coverage varies by agency — verify as_of and agency participation before relying on any figure.

Aggregate agency/location statistics only — named sex-offender registries and any per-person records are deliberately excluded; never returns data about identifiable people. Output is a RISK INDICATOR, not a consumer report, and NOT for tenant/employment/insurance/credit decisions in violation of the Fair Housing Act, ECOA or FCRA.
usage.guide: Get an FBI reporting agency's normalized crime profile in one paid call when you already hold its ORI code. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/crime/agency?ori=<ORI> (optionally &offense=<offense>&years=<n>). Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base. Returns the agency identity plus per-year offense rates per 100,000 people (annualized from FBI UCR/NIBRS monthly data), which years are complete, the trend from the earliest to latest complete year, and the data as-of date. Use crime/location instead if you only have an address/place and need the geocode-to-agency step. Verified live at index time: paid $0.01 -> HTTP 200 for ori=DE0010100 (offense=violent-crime); the upstream FBI source was briefly returning 403, so the response came back as a valid partial envelope (sources.partial=true, empty annual_rates) — the route, schema and payment all confirmed working.

entries.name: Agentstools Travel Advisory

destination.description: Destination country as a name, ISO2 or ISO3 code, e.g. 'France', 'FR' or 'FRA'.
Resolved destination country (echoes the normalized ISO2/ISO3/name for the input).

found.description: Whether a State Department advisory record was found for the destination.

level.description: Advisory level 1–4 (1=Exercise Normal Precautions … 4=Do Not Travel).

advisory.description: The advisory payload, or null when found is false.

partial.description: True if one or more upstream sources failed for this query.

usage.outputShape: destination{iso2,iso3,name} (resolved country), found (bool), advisory{level (1-4), level_label, updated, source} | null, sources{providers[], errors{per-provider}, partial (bool)}, attribution[] (US Dept of State — travel.state.gov, public domain), disclaimer.

Sources the US State Department travel advisories (travel.state.gov, public domain), normalized to one cited JSON with an advisory level 1–4 and label.

The endpoint always returns its full documented shape with HTTP 200 even when no advisory is found: at index time (2026-08-07) the paid call for destination='France' resolved the country correctly (iso2 FR, iso3 FRA) but returned found=false, advisory=null and an empty sources.providers[] — the upstream advisory source returned no record this run (sources.partial=false, no errors), similar to the transient-upstream-degradation pattern seen on sibling Agentstools openFDA ops. The 402 bazaar example shows the populated shape (level 2 'Exercise Increased Caution', updated 2024-01-08).

Informational only — per the response disclaimer this is NOT immigration, visa or legal advice and NOT a guarantee of entry; verify with the destination's embassy/immigration authority before travelling.
usage.guide: Look up the current US State Department travel advisory for a destination with a single keyless x402 GET. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/travel/advisory?destination=<country name, ISO2 or ISO3 code> (e.g. destination=France or destination=FR). No request body. Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base. Synchronous — the 200 body carries the resolved destination{iso2,iso3,name}, found (bool), advisory{level 1-4, level_label, updated, source} (or null when not found), sources{providers, errors, partial}, plus US Dept of State attribution and a disclaimer. destination.description: Destination country name, ISO2 or ISO3 code (e.g. 'Uganda', 'UG', 'UGA')
{ iso2, iso3, name } for the resolved destination country

entries.name: Agentstools Answer
entries.description: Cited retrieval-augmented answer to a natural-language question — searches the public web, reads the top pages and synthesizes a concise grounded answer that cites ONLY the retrieved sources with inline [n] markers (anti-hallucination). Pay-per-call x402.

backends.inputSchema: GET query params: query (string, REQUIRED — the natural-language question to answer), max_sources (integer 1-5, optional, default 3 — how many top web pages to read/cite), timelimit (string enum d/w/m/y — freshness: past day/week/month/year, optional), region (string locale like 'us-en','uk-en'; default us-en, optional). No request body.
backends.outputSchema: { query (string, echoed), answer (string — synthesized answer with inline [n] citation markers), sources[]: { url (string), title (string) }, used_sources[] (string urls actually cited), model (string — synthesis model). May also return insufficient:true when nothing relevant is found, or synthesis_available:false (sources only) when synthesis is momentarily unavailable. }

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/answer?query=what%20is%20the%20x402%20payment%20protocol&max_sources=3&timelimit=w (query REQUIRED; max_sources 1-5/timelimit d|w|m|y/region optional; all query-string params, no request body)

inputExample.query: what is the x402 payment protocol

usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. body.query echoes the question, body.answer is the synthesized answer text with inline [n] markers, body.sources[] lists the retrieved pages ({url,title}), body.used_sources[] lists the source urls actually cited, and body.model names the synthesis model. Always a valid HTTP 200: if nothing relevant is found it returns insufficient:true; if synthesis is momentarily unavailable it returns the sources with synthesis_available:false (never a 5xx).

The answer is grounded: an anti-hallucination prompt forbids outside knowledge, so it cites ONLY the retrieved sources with inline [n] markers.
Always returns HTTP 200 (never a 5xx): insufficient:true means no relevant results; synthesis_available:false means the sources came back but synthesis was momentarily down.
max_sources is capped at 5.
The observed synthesis model was 'deepseek-chat' (the openapi example shows 'deepseek-v4-flash') — treat the model field as provider-chosen and variable.

Partial-success mode: a down upstream degrades to sources.partial=true with sources.errors[] populated rather than failing. Retry when partial.

usage.guide: Get a factual profile of one team in a major sports league (MLB, NHL, NFL, NBA or the English Premier League) in one keyless paid call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/sports/team?league=<mlb|nhl|nfl|nba|epl>&team=<name-or-abbr> (name is an accepted alias for team; league is required). Pays $0.005 USDC via x402 on Base, no API key. Synchronous — read the 200 JSON directly: found, team.{team,abbr,sport,venue,country,founded,record,source}, provenance, sources, attribution[], disclaimer. Handle found:false (unresolved team) and sources.partial=true (a source degraded) — both return HTTP 200. Preserve attribution[] and disclaimer (facts fused from official league APIs, ESPN and TheSportsDB; informational only, not affiliated with any league, no odds). Deterministic, no LLM.
